text:
maya: Heads up — saw repeated create/destroy churn of GPU nodepools in us-west-2 overnight. ~3 cycles in 6h. Apps hit OOM/pending pods briefly.
aj: ugh. any obvious error in the operator logs?
maya: helmfile sync job failed on the 2nd apply with a remote state conflict in our terraform repo. infra job retried and the terraform apply ended up replacing the nodepool instead of patching labels.
rob: can you paste the plan or error? sounds like drift + replace.
maya: sure. infra-bot captured this from CI:

```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 1 changed, 2 destroyed.

Note: the nodepool resource had a `force_replace = true` in a generated module due to name change.
```

rob: that explains the replace. We should not be allowing auto-generated name changes from helm values. Which pipeline mutated values? helmfile or terraform module inputs?
maya: looks like helmfile renders chart-values that feed into the infra repo via the kustomize->tf var generation job. There was a small refactor to node naming -> `${cluster}-${gpuType}-${env}` which changed string construction.

sasha: real quick — were we using the cluster-autoscaler or a custom provisioner? CA behaves weird with node replacement and pending GPU pods.
aj: cluster-autoscaler (CA). The CA sees the nodepool gone and deschedules; pending pods accumulate until replacement finished. Cost impact and availability hit.

rob: two-pronged fix: (1) stop churn by reverting naming change and pinning nodepool name in tf vars, (2) change apply workflow so terraform can't do destructive replaces without human review.
maya: +1. Propose adding a preflight check in the helmfile->tf generator to diff nodepool names and fail the pipeline if name changes are detected. Also add a `prevent_destroy` lifecycle block for gpu nodepools in terraform.

aj: lifecycle prevent_destroy will block legitimate deletes though. Maybe better to add `ignore_changes = ["node_count"]`? hmm.
rob: `prevent_destroy` for prod gpu pools only, and for non-prod we can allow. Also adopt `create_before_destroy = false`? Wait we want create_before_destroy = true for minimal downtime but that can double cost temporarily.
sasha: another option: change autoscaler config to prefer `expander: least-waste` and tune `scaleDownUnneededTime` so CA doesn't kill nodes midway. But that won't stop tf replacing pools.
maya: infra-bot suggestion:

```
resources:
  - type: aws_eks_node_group
    lifecycle:
      prevent_destroy: true
      create_before_destroy: false
```

infra-bot: automated note — I flagged the terraform workspace run as partial-fail and left a lock token. Manual unlock performed by @rob at 02:14 UTC.

rob: thanks infra-bot. I'm opening a quick PR to revert the naming change and add a guard in the generator: if generated nodepool_name != state.nodepool_name then fail and open a draft PR instead of applying.

aj: while you're at it, can we add an integration test that runs `terraform plan` in dry-run mode and fails CI if it would replace >0 gpu nodepool resources? That would have caught this.

maya: yes — terraform plan + grep for "-/+" and resource type filter. Example (very rough):

```
terraform plan -out=plan.out && terraform show -json plan.out | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.type=="aws_eks_node_group") | {address,change}'
```

sasha: ops playbook note: if you see nodepool replace in prod, set CA scale down to 15m and disable scale-down for affected ASGs until replacement completes. Also pre-warm capacity in secondary pool with same labels to avoid pending GPU pods.

rob: Opening PR: r/infrastructure#412 — revert naming + add plan guard + docs for runbook. Will add patch for `helmfile -> tf var gen` too.

maya: post-PR checklist: 1) block helmfile sync until manual approval 2) run plan check job 3) verify no destructive changes in the plan 4) merge revert

aj: timeline? this morning we hit two incidents. If PR lands in next 1-2 hours we can avoid tonight's batch run.

rob: targeting merge in 45min. I'll also add a non-blocking alert to #oncall when CA sees >3 node churn events in 1h.
maya: thanks. Also can we add an annotation `redwood/gpu-provisioned-by: manual` to prod pools to make accidental automation less likely? small label but big ROI.

sasha: agreed. one last callout — update cost dashboard to show temporary double-capacity events so finance can be tagged.

infra-bot: reminder: next scheduled helmfile->terraform sync is at 03:00 UTC. It has been paused by rob.

rob: leaving a calendar note. I'll post PR link when ready.

maya: thx — will monitor node events and CA metrics. ping here if anything else pops up. :eyes:
